definition: 2031 milestone on the Living Material Panels 2.0 roadmap.
description:

What must be true first: the cell scaffolds results have to replicate outside the lab, panel logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and cell feeding operations need a year of continuous runtime. Signals to watch: peer-reviewed cell scaffolds demonstrations, panel logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting cell feeding uptime. When all three flash green, 2031 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (5 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Living Material Panels 2.0
definition: Estimates Living Material Panels 2.0 readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Living Material Panels 2.0 components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a panel hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Living Material Panels 2.0 Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Living Material Panels 2.0 operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Living Material Panels 2.0 installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 36863 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where cell scaffolds monitoring, panel logistics redundancy, or cell feeding maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Living Material Panels 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Living Material Panels 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Living Material Panels 2.0 — next-gen panels with living cells inside.

Phase 1 — Prove (cell scaffolds): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (panel logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (cell feeding): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (response behaviors): panel hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and architecture-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
